title: Two-block Schur factorization and determinant identity over a commutative ring
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring and let $a,b\geq0$. Let $P,Q,T,W$ be matrices over $R$ of sizes $a\times a$, $a\times b$, $b\times a$, $b\times b$, respectively [def-weil-matrix]. Suppose $P$ has a two-sided inverse $P^{-1}$. Put $S=W-TP^{-1}Q$. With determinant as in [def-weil-pbc-matrix-determinant], one has
$$\begin{pmatrix}P&Q\\ T&W\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}I_a&0\\ TP^{-1}&I_b\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}P&0\\0&S\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}I_a&P^{-1}Q\\0&I_b\end{pmatrix},\qquad \det\begin{pmatrix}P&Q\\ T&W\end{pmatrix}=\det(P)\det(S).$$
The identities include $a=0$, $b=0$, and the zero ring; the empty determinant is $1$.
